Working notes: order intake
- Required form v1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Each intake batch is an attempt (1–3). After 3 rejected attempts, record goes to manual review; move to next.
- Accepted outcome (+1.00); rejected outcome (-0.20) lists invalid fields. Use prior invalid-field list to target next attempt, but recheck all fields—previously valid fields can regress if omitted.
- Never submit empty/partial did. Carry forward known valid cust/email/order_date. Logs truncate did; missing from displayed JSON is not proof.
- Priority is the most common invalid field (nearly every rejection). Ship_country often invalid; qty sometimes. cust/email/order_date usually valid when present.
- Source reliability: "Customer called to confirm"/phone typed can fix some fields (e.g., ship_country) but not priority. Handwritten transcription and emailed orders vary; partner portal not automatically reliable.
- Observed: Dee Reyes ORD-5106 rejected priority, ship_country; ORD-5107 accepted after corrections. Eli Okafor ORD-5109 still invalid priority after ship_country fixed. Bo Okafor ORD-5104 invalid priority only; ORD-5105 empty/partial rejected cust/email/qty/ship_country—preserve valid fields.
- Strategy: extract all six fields from full source; on retry fix previous invalid fields; preserve prior valid fields; ensure complete before final attempt.

Working notes: order intake
- Form v1 required: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Batch attempts 1–3. After 3 rejected attempts: manual review, next record.
- Accepted +1.00; rejected -0.20 lists invalid fields. Use prior invalid list to target next attempt, but recheck all fields—previously valid fields can regress if omitted.
- Never submit empty/partial did. Carry forward known valid cust/email/order_date. Logs truncate did; missing from displayed JSON is not proof.
- Priority remains most common invalid (nearly every rejection). Ship_country often invalid; qty sometimes. cust/email/order_date usually valid when present. Empty did often flags cust/email/qty/ship_country (priority not listed).
- Voicemail transcriptions are often incomplete, usually yield only cust/email/order_date; priority/ship_country frequently fail. Emailed orders vary. Partner portal not automatically reliable. Front-desk notes (“duplicate check”, “ordinary priority”, “called to confirm”) are not reliable fixes, especially priority/ship_country.
- Observed: ORD-5110 Eli Okafor attempt 3 rejected ship_country only. ORD-5111/5114 empty did rejected cust/email/qty/ship_country. ORD-5112/5115/5116/5117/5118/5119 priority often invalid, often with ship_country. ORD-5113 partner portal attempt 3 rejected priority+ship_country.
- Strategy: extract all six fields from full source; on retry fix previous invalid fields; preserve prior valid fields; ensure complete before final attempt.

Working notes (updated step 39)

Order form v1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. All must be present and parseable.

Recent experience:
- ORD-5130–5139 all rejected (-0.20). Invalid fields consistently priority plus qty and/or ship_country.
- Root cause: source records are truncated/incomplete. Emailed/pasted JSON cuts off after order_date/pri; voicemail transcriptions also cut off. Missing tail fields cannot be inferred.
- Examples: Cy Reyes (user792, 2026-08-23); Bo Sato (user622, 2026-07-28); Ada Marsh (user590, 2026-09-22); Eli Marsh (user599, 2026-03-14). All affected.
- Attempts 1–3 on the same malformed source do not fix missing fields; outcomes repeat. After attempt 3, record goes to manual review.
- Forwarder, intake note, duplicate-check claim, and form version do not compensate for an incomplete source.

Decision guidance:
- For form v1, validate the full source parse before submission: priority, qty, ship_country must be explicitly present.
- If source ends before these fields (truncated JSON, voicemail cut off), expect rejection; do not rely on retries to recover data.
- Retry only if a new/complete source is provided. Otherwise flag/route for manual review.
- Do not infer priority, qty, or ship_country from customer name, email, order_date, or intake comments.

New examples confirm: Bo Sato (user700, 2026-11-09), Dee Okafor (user926, 2026-08-08), Cy Sato (user997, 2026-03-20), Eli Marsh (user599, 2026-03-14). Same-name records vary; use email/source, not name.

- If the source ends before these fields (truncated JSON, voicemail cut off), expect rejection; do not retry the same source.
- Retry only with a new/complete source. Otherwise flag/route for manual review.
- Do not infer priority, qty, or ship_country from cust, email, order_date, intake comments, or front-desk notes.

Form v1 needs cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country; all must parse.

Pattern: ORD-5130–5159 rejected (-0.20). Invalid fields are priority and ship_country almost always; qty is also invalid in some (ORD-5150–5152, 5156–5158) but not all (ORD-5153–5155, 5159).
